subject: Re: DTIA artifacts and control mapping for UK Addendum
messages:
From: Sara Horton <sara.horton@tempo-thera.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: DTIA artifacts and control mapping for UK Addendum

Hi Kimberly / Marissa —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Tempo's legal and security teams are compiling the final list of artifacts we need to close our DTIA (data transfer impact assessment) and to sign the UK Addendum. To make the internal review efficient, can you provide the following by end of week?

- A compact control mapping (CSV/XLSX) that maps Redwood controls to the TIA/DTIA checklist items we discussed (encryption in transit, at-rest key custody, subprocessor egress, logging retention, incident response SLA).
- A network diagram that highlights any cross-border egress points and third-party transfer hops (edge/CDN, batch export endpoints).
- Sample logs (redacted) or a description of retention windows and PHI/PII masking for transfers.
- Confirmation of whether the UK Addendum we discussed is the one with the conditional proxy-processing carve-out (we have a draft to run through DocuSign once controls are confirmed).

If you prefer, we can accept a short matrix + one diagram and then follow with a separate package for logs. Our legal team wants language tied back to specific control owners (e.g., "Key management: Infra / KMS team").

Appreciate the fast turn — Jonas from Redwood security was looped in for any technical clarifications.

Best,
Sara Horton
Senior Counsel, Tempo Therapeutics
---
Tempo Therapeutics | sara.horton@tempo-thera.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Horton <sara.horton@tempo-thera.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DTIA artifacts and control mapping for UK Addendum

Sara —

Thanks for the clear list. We can get a consolidated package to you by Friday EOD. High-level plan below so you can share with legal/security: 

1) Control matrix (attached: control-matrix.xlsx) — maps Redwood controls to DTIA items. Columns include: DTIA clause, Redwood control ID, control owner (team), evidence type, evidence pointer (Drive link).
2) Network diagram (attached: redwood-network-diagram.png) — shows external ingress/egress, Cloud region routing rules, and where on-prem dedicated clusters (if applicable) may touch data.
3) Logs & retention summary — we will include a redacted sample log snippet and a short table describing log types, retention, and access controls. Full logs are available under MSA/PoV constraints; we can provide extracts for audited items.
4) UK Addendum draft — attached a marked-up copy for signature readiness. Legal review note: the Addendum template we referenced includes the conditional processing proxy carve-out; I called out the exact section in the matrix (row C-12).

Jonas — can you confirm the encryption and egress language in rows C-3 and C-7 of the spreadsheet? Marissa, I left a couple of procurement notes in the Drive link about the DocuSign cadence.

Attachments: control-matrix.xlsx (matrix), redwood-network-diagram.png (diagram), uk-addendum-draft-for-signature.pdf (draft).

Thanks — will follow up with a short recording explaining the matrix.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Legal Ops (Data & Privacy)
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0132

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Horton <sara.horton@tempo-thera.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DTIA artifacts and control mapping for UK Addendum

Kimberly / Marissa / Sara —

Quick technical notes after reviewing the attached matrix: 

- Row C-3 (encryption in transit): we affirm TLS1.2+ with cipher suites that meet NIST recommendations; for long-tail connectors we can provide an mTLS option upon request. I added a note in the matrix to reference the cert rotation cadence.
- Row C-7 (subprocessor egress controls): Redwood enforces egress restrictions at the routing layer for hosted API requests; any export/backup jobs that might cross regions are handled by scheduled batch workers under dedicated accounts — we have SOC2-tested processes for the export path. However, Tempo's legal asked for explicit "egress approval" paperwork for scheduled exports. We can offer a three-way approval flow (Tempo PO -> Redwood Data Ops -> Redwood Security) recorded in the audit trail.
- Logs: we will provide a redacted sample and a schema for the audit events (authentication, request path, model id, region, byte counts). Retention defaults: 90 days for request logs, 365 days for security event logs; retention policy can be adjusted under contract for enterprise/private deployments.
- Network diagram ask: could you confirm whether your compliance team needs the ASN-level egress hops or the higher-level region/CDN view? I can produce both but ASN-level will take extra time.

My only ask before we hand this back: can Kim/legal confirm the exact wording Tempo wants in the UK Addendum for the proxy-processing carve-out? There are two variants: (A) affirmative carve-out with explicit processor-to-processor transfer authorization vs (B) conditional language that requires pre-approval for certain categories. For speed, we can prepare redlines for both.

Jonas Weber
Lead, Product Security
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Horton <sara.horton@tempo-thera.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2026 15:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DTIA artifacts and control mapping for UK Addendum

Kim / Jonas —

Appreciate the rapid turnaround and the attachments. Tempo legal reviewed the matrix and asked for two small clarifications before we prepare the DocuSign packet: 

1) Please add the KMS provider and key separation model to C-4 (we only need vendor name and whether keys are customer-managed or Redwood-managed).
2) For the egress approval flow, could you confirm an expected SLA to process approval requests ("approval processed within X business days") and whether approvals create an immutable audit record we can reference?

If you can add those two items, we should be ready to execute the UK Addendum next week. When you send the update, I'll circulate to Tempo's CTO and our procurement lead and kick off the DocuSign envelope (DocuSign:1234-UK-ADDENDUM-REQ).

Thanks again — small closing asks, then we can finish the DTIA sign-off.

Best,
Sara Horton
Senior Counsel, Tempo Therapeutics
